subject: Data residency & model training assurances — deletion and retention details

Subject: Questions on training usage + deletion process

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and security teams about how Redwood handles customer data, specifically: 

1) Do you ever use customer request/data to continue training or fine-tune Redwood models (either internal or public models)?
2) If not, what are the retention windows for logs, request/response payloads, and backups? Are there differences between Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments?
3) What is the deletion workflow when we request complete deletion (and how do you handle backups / snapshots / disaster-recovery copies)?

Our concern: we handle regulated financial data and we need contractual assurances that nothing will be used for model training and that deletion is effective within a definable timeframe. Can you share the typical SLAs and any exceptions (e.g., legal hold)?

Could you point the security team to a short FAQ or whitepaper and ideally a named contact to coordinate for procurement?

Appreciate it — looking forward to the details.

— Paula

Hi Paula — looping in some technical specifics below. I'll keep it practical and call out exceptions.

1) Training usage: 
- We DO NOT use customer request/response payloads from Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments to train or fine-tune any Redwood public models by default. For Hosted and Dedicated customers, we retain telemetry and aggregated usage metrics (e.g., token counts, latency histograms) for platform improvement, but these are not payloads.
- Opt-in: customers can opt into a data-sharing program (explicit written agreement) to allow sanitized/aggregated examples to be used for model improvement. This is never automatic.

2) Retention windows (typical defaults):
- Hosted API: request/response payloads (full text) retained for 30 days by default to support debugging and abuse detection; logs/metrics for 13 months aggregated.
- Dedicated: default retention of request/response payloads is 90 days; customers can shorten or extend retention via config and contractual terms.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): retention is customer-configurable; Redwood-managed control plane retains only minimal metadata unless otherwise negotiated.

Notes on backups/snapshots:
- Backups and autoscaling snapshots may contain encrypted metadata; full request payload backups are not kept longer than the configured retention period. In Hosted, snapshots used for infra recovery are rotated and expire — they are not used for model training.

3) Deletion workflow and guarantees: 
- Deletion request (self-serve API or support ticket) initiates: mark data for deletion -> remove from active stores -> purge from caches -> schedule deletion from backups.
- Typical purge completion: Hosted API — within 30 days plus a short buffer for backup rotation; Dedicated — configurable, typically 30–90 days depending on snapshot schedules; Private — depends on customer's on-prem retention policies and whether Redwood has a managed control plane.
- Exceptions: legal hold, subpoena, or other lawful process will pause deletion; we will notify the customer per contract.

4) Additional safeguards and contractual language: 
- No-training clause: We provide a contractual clause stating Redwood will not train on customer-provided content (requests/responses) unless the customer provides explicit, documented consent.
- Auditability: for Dedicated and Private customers we can provide audit logs showing deletion operations and retention config changes.
- Security controls: KMS integration, optional HSM, TLS in transit, encryption at rest, and SOC2-compliant processes.

5) Timeline / SLA 
- Deletion acknowledgement: 48 business hours after validated request.
- Completion confirmation: per retention schedule (see above).
- We can include stricter SLAs in the DPA for enterprise deals.

If helpful, Laura can prepare a short one-page DPA excerpt showing the explicit "no training" language and the retention/delete timelines we will commit to. If you want the technical call, I can be available Tue–Thu next week in the morning PST.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
